question: How do intrinsic dimensionality and neighborhood geometry evolve across transformer depth, training, and scale, and where do semantically richest representations occur?

key_findings.claim: Large self-supervised transformers show a nonmonotonic layerwise intrinsic-dimension profile rather than steady compression.
key_findings.evidence: Two-nearest-neighbor estimates on ESM-2 protein models and iGPT image models exhibit early expansion, contraction to a relative minimum, and later plateau or secondary rise. The pattern recurs across several model sizes and related protein architectures.

anchors.section: Appendix C other protein language models

key_findings.claim: Successive-layer neighbor overlap reveals periods of rapid geometric rearrangement that coincide with major changes in intrinsic dimension.
key_findings.evidence: The fraction of shared nearest neighbors between adjacent layers falls during transformative portions of the stack and rises in more stable regions, distinguishing dimension change from mere coordinate reparameterization.

key_findings.claim: During pretraining the characteristic profile develops progressively rather than being fixed by architecture alone.
key_findings.evidence: ESM-2 checkpoints show the expansion peak and later contraction becoming pronounced with training, while untrained/early models lack the mature geometry. Size affects magnitude and detail but not the overall qualitative phases.

key_findings.claim: External semantic-neighbor overlap is maximal near a relative intrinsic-dimension minimum, suggesting an unsupervised layer-selection heuristic.
key_findings.evidence: Remote protein-homology labels and image semantics align most strongly with representations around the compressed middle/late region rather than necessarily the final layer. Labels are used only for validation, while ID could in principle choose the layer without labels.

anchors.section: 4 Local geometry and semantic relations / Figure 4

method.core_idea: Use local intrinsic dimension and nearest-neighbor overlap as label-free probes of representational expansion, reorganization, compression, and semantic concentration through depth.
method.mechanism: Sequence representations are pooled into vectors for each hidden layer. The TwoNN ratio of first- to second-neighbor distances estimates global intrinsic dimension; k-neighbor overlap compares adjacent layers or hidden geometry with external semantic relations. Profiles are traced across model sizes and training checkpoints.
assumptions: Local samples approximate a manifold with density smooth enough for the TwoNN estimator.
Average pooling preserves the representation geometry relevant to protein/image semantics.
Euclidean nearest neighbors are meaningful and sufficiently stable in the sampled hidden spaces.
ESM-2 and iGPT support conclusions about self-supervised transformers beyond these modalities.

techniques.role: Estimates local manifold dimension from minimal nearest-neighbor information.
Measures how strongly each block rearranges local geometry.
Validates where geometry aligns with remote homology or class structure.
Separates architectural shape from structure acquired through training.

evaluations.setting: ESM-2 protein transformers at 35M, 650M, and 3B parameters plus other protein language-model architectures.
evaluations.metric: Layerwise TwoNN intrinsic dimension and neighbor overlap.
evaluations.result: Models share expansion-contraction structure, with scale-dependent details and stable replication across related architectures.
evaluations.baseline: Input embeddings, final layers, smaller models, and other protein transformers.

evaluations.setting: iGPT image transformers of different sizes.
evaluations.metric: Intrinsic-dimension profile and layerwise neighborhood rearrangement.
evaluations.result: A qualitatively similar nonmonotonic geometry appears outside language/protein data, supporting but not proving modality generality.

evaluations.setting: Protein remote-homology and image semantic labels used as post hoc validation.
evaluations.metric: Overlap between hidden-space neighbors and ground-truth semantic neighbors.
evaluations.result: Peak semantic organization occurs near a relative ID minimum, often before the final layer.

limitations: Only two principal self-supervised model families and modalities are deeply tested.
Average pooling can erase token- or patch-local geometry and alters dimension estimates.
TwoNN relies on local density/manifold assumptions and is sensitive to sample size and metric concentration.
Semantic labels validate correlation but do not explain why compression produces useful representations.
Global ID averages can hide class- or region-specific manifold structure.
failure_modes: Nearest-neighbor instability in high ambient dimension can generate spurious ID peaks.
A low-dimensional bottleneck can discard information rather than concentrate semantics.
Pooling or normalization choices can shift the apparent optimal layer.
Domain shift can move semantic quality away from the layer selected on the pretraining corpus.
reusable_insights: Layer selection should be treated as an empirical geometry problem rather than defaulting to the final layer.
Combine dimension with neighbor turnover: the same ID can conceal very different geometric transformations.
Checkpoint profiles help distinguish representations learned by optimization from biases fixed by architecture.
open_questions: Does the ID-minimum heuristic select useful layers across generative LLM tasks and prompt distributions?
Can token-local or conditional intrinsic dimension reveal mechanisms hidden by pooled global estimates?
What training objective causes the late-stage expansion or secondary peak, and is it beneficial?

competitive_landscape.title: Estimating the intrinsic dimension of datasets by a minimal neighborhood information
competitive_landscape.relationship: Introduces the TwoNN estimator used to measure the hidden representation manifolds.
competitive_landscape.difference: The original work develops and validates the estimator on general data; this paper applies it layerwise to large transformers and relates its minima to semantic organization.

competitive_landscape.title: Layer by Layer: Uncovering Hidden Representations in Language Models
competitive_landscape.relationship: Uses information, geometry, and perturbation metrics over depth and evaluates mid-layer embeddings on 32 downstream tasks.
competitive_landscape.difference: It provides a much broader task-based language-model evaluation; the 2023 paper offers an earlier intrinsic-dimension/neighborhood account in protein and image transformers with checkpoint evolution.

competitive_landscape.title: Learning to Compress: Local Rank and Information Compression in Deep Neural Networks
competitive_landscape.relationship: Studies local rank and information compression as representations propagate through deep networks.
competitive_landscape.difference: It develops a local-rank compression perspective; this work uses TwoNN plus neighborhood overlap and directly validates transformer layers against protein/image semantics.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: Large self-supervised transformers exhibit a shared geometric learning pattern in which semantic information concentrates near an intrinsic-dimension minimum.
novelty_assessment.evidence: Profiles replicate over scales, checkpoints, protein architectures, and an image-transformer family, with semantic-neighbor overlap peaking in the predicted region.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The cross-modality profile and unsupervised layer heuristic are compelling; the limited model families and estimator assumptions prevent a universal geometry claim.
